headline: Hyperlane: Permissionless interoperability protocol across 150+ chains; deployed addresses discoverable via registry and explorer; multiple audits by Trail of Bits, Zellic, Hacken, Sec3, ChainLight, and others
short_headline: Cross-chain messaging protocol across 150+ chains with multiple audits

findings.text: Hyperlane is a prominent permissionless interoperability protocol with verified name tags on major block explorers; Mailbox proxy identified on Optimism at 0xd4c1905bb1d26bc93dac913e13cacc278cdcc80d; HYPER governance token deployed on Ethereum (0x93a2db22b7c736b341c32ff666307f4a9ed910f5).

Hyperlane registry available at https://github.com/hyperlane-xyz/hyperlane-registry with config artifacts, chains metadata, and warp route deployments; canonical documentation at https://docs.hyperlane.xyz with deployment guides referencing registry as source of chain metadata.

12 audit reports documented across multiple security firms: Trail of Bits (Protocol v3), Hacken (Protocol v2), FYEO (Protocol v1), Sec3 (Sealevel), ChainLight (Q2 2025, HyperToken, Yield Routes, CCIP v5.12.0, Hook/ISM), Oak Security (CosmWasm), Offbeat (Compound Staker Rewards), ChainSecurity (USDT), and Sherlock (Sealevel). All accessible via https://docs.hyperlane.xyz/docs/resources/audits.

GitHub organization at https://github.com/hyperlane-xyz with primary repository hyperlane-monorepo (core contracts), hyperlane-deploy (deployment scripts), hyperlane-registry (deployment artifacts and configs), and 60+ repositories. Deployment scripts and artifacts stored in standardized Foundry broadcast format per chain.

Protocol is deployed across 25+ specified chains: Ethereum, Binance, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, Avalanche, Linea, Blast, Scroll, Mantle, xDai, Mode, Metis, BSquared, Ink, Plasma, Hyperliquid L1, Unichain, Zora, Mint, Celo, Sei, Sonic, Vana, Swellchain. Each deployment registered in hyperlane-registry with chain-specific metadata.

Hyperlane enables permissionless warp routes (token bridges) across chains; factory-pattern deployments identified in documentation and audit reports. Core protocol instances one-per-chain (Mailbox, ISM contracts) with warp route instances unlimited per chain.

Admin control structures: Mailbox contracts use OpenZeppelin Ownable pattern; ISMs and hooks customizable by app developers; validators run off-chain agents; relayers operate permissionlessly; protocol uses modular security with developer-selectable ISM (multisig, optimistic, merkle, etc.).

All address discoveries traced to fetched URLs: official website, documentation, public GitHub repositories, and audit reports. Block explorer name-tagged instances (Optimism Mailbox) confirmed via Etherscan/optimistic.etherscan.io links in search results.

rationale.verdict: Discovery phase: Hyperlane is a well-documented cross-chain messaging protocol with extensive on-chain presence across 25+ chains, comprehensive audit history from reputable firms, and a structured deployment registry. Key artifacts identified: primary GitHub org (hyperlane-xyz), canonical documentation (docs.hyperlane.xyz), audit reports (12 reports documented), and governance token (HYPER on Ethereum). Downstream control/autonomy/verifiability slices will need to enumerate specific mailbox admin addresses per chain, validate ISM/hook architecture, and audit dates.

protocol_metadata.about: Hyperlane is a permissionless interoperability layer enabling cross-chain messaging across 150+ blockchains and 7 virtual machines (EVM, Solana, Cosmos, Starknet, CosmWasm, Sealevel, custom). Developers deploy Mailbox contracts to any chain and configure modular Interchain Security Modules (ISMs) to customize message verification. The protocol supports Warp Routes for permissionless token bridging, interchain accounts, and arbitrary message passing, with a permissionless validator/relayer network secured by HYPER token staking.
